sentences.text: It is settled proposition of law that an action founded SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK MACT No.213/2018 Date: 2024.02.16 16:04:14 +0530 Page 3 on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the claim petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others.

sentences.text: 11 . Petitioner (PW1) in his deposition has stated that on 10.07.2017 while he was driving his motorcycle, he was hit from behind by tractor trolley no.DL-1E-2115, when it was being driven by respondent no.1 in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner.
PW1 further stated that he noted down registration number of offending vehicle and called the police at 100 number.
Nothing came in the cross examination of PW1 except mere suggestions from respondents.

As such the evidence of PW1 is cogent and convincing regarding involvement of tractor no.DL-1E-2115 and regarding rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
12.
Respondent no.1 appeared as R1W1 and has testified that no accident took place from his tractor no.DL-1E- 2115 on 10.07.2017.
R1W1 further says that he is innocent and falsely implicated in FIR No.260/2017.
Evidence of R1W1 can SHAILENDER MALIK MACT No.213/2018

MALIK Date:
2024.02.16 Page 4 16:04:22 +0530 hardly be of any reliance as witness in cross examination states that he is not aware about the contents of his affidavit.
Witness further says that he is not aware any FIR was registered against him.
R1W1 however admits that he was arrested by the police and criminal case regarding the accident in question is pending against him.
He further admits that he has never filed any protest petition or representation regarding his alleged false implication in criminal case.

13. Similarly evidence of R2W1 who also simply denied about the accident from tractor no.DL-1E-2115, can be of no relevance as R2W1 admits that he was served notice u/s 133 M.V. Act and produced the driver/respondent no.1.
He further admits that vehicle no.DL-1E-2115 was seized by the police and he got it released on superdari.

14. Thus considering the evidence as come on the judicial record, this Tribunal finds that evidence of PW1 is specific and cogent, gets corroboration from the documents filed with DAR including report u/s 173 Cr.PC, seizure memo, notice u/s 133 M.V. Act, site plan as well as mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle.
As such it can safely be concluded that accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of driver/respondent no.1 while driving tractor no.DL-1E-2115.
Accordingly issue stands decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.

sentences.text: The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.

entities.text: R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant extract is as under:
SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK MACT No.213/2018 Page 5 Date:
2024.02.16 16:04:34 +0530 "Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.

So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned, they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future;
(ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience,
discomfort, disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life."
16.
Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:
4.

The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.

The object of awarding SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK MACT No.213/2018 Page 6 Date: 2024.02.16 16:04:43 +0530 damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

sentences.text:
The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.

Non-Pecuniary Damages (general  damages)
 (iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of  prospects of marriage)
 (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date:
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.

17. In the light of the aforementioned judgments, the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled shall be as under:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Medical Expenses:

PW1 in his deposition stated that after the accident he was taken to GTB Hospital where his MLC was prepared and he suffered multiple fractures on his right leg beside multiple abrasions on other parts of body.

PW1 stated that he has been working as taxi driver and took treatment in GTB Hospital, Arogya Hospital, Vaishali,
Ghaziabad.

As such his claim is only for Rs.3,305/- regarding medical expenses.
19. Above noted facts as come in the evidence of PW1 were submitted by the counsel for the petitioner.
Taking into SHAILENDER MALIK MACT No.213/2018

MALIK Date:
2024.02.16 Page 8 16:04:59 +0530 consideration the medical bills, nature of injuries,
since most of the medical expenses/bills have already been reimbursed to petitioner.
There being no dispute with regard to claim of petitioner for sum of Rs.3,305/- for medical expenses, therefore this Tribunal awards medical expenses for Rs.3,305/- to the petitioner.

Loss of earning during treatment:
20. Petitioner/ PW1 has testified that he has been working as taxi driver and is otherwise educated upto 12th standard.

Although petitioner claims that he has been earning as taxi driver Rs.15,000/- per month, however PW1 admits in his cross- examination that he has not filed any income document or employment documents.
PW1 further admits that he does not have any commercial driving licence.

21. In the absence of any evidence to show that petitioner was working as driver or was earning Rs.15,000/- as claimed by him, considering the evidence of PW1 this Tribunal is of considered view that income of petitioner is to be assessed at parity with minimum wages of skilled worker as prevailing in Delhi at the time of accident i.e. Rs.16,182/- per month.

22. Now moving ahead, from the medical documents of Arogya Hospital, GTB Hospital it is very much evident that after the accident petitioner initially received treatment in GTB Hospital and later in Arogya Hospital.
Petitioner was admitted in Arogya Hospital on 20.07.2017 and discharged on 23.07.2017.

It also came in the evidence of PW2 that medical condition of the petitioner was assessed by medical board of GTB Hospital whereby it was found that petitioner was permanently disabled for 25% in relation to left lower limb.

As such taking into SHAILENDER MALIK MACT No.213/2018 MALIK Date: 2024.02.16 16:05:09 +0530 Page 9 consideration the medical documents, nature of injuries i.e. multiple fractures and abrasions, it can be concluded that petitioner remained confined to bed for treatment for about two months.

As such petitioner is Dar- Sonu Gautam vs Avadhveer Singh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43808257/
6 entitled for sum of Rs.32,364/- (Rs.16,182 X 2) for loss of earning during treatment.

sentences.text:
Loss of future earning due to disability :
23.

In case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India determined the broad criteria for assessment of permanent disability for ascertaining the purpose of future loss of earning and also laid down step by step procedure for assessment of disability and for ascertainment to the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:-
"9.
Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so, the extent of such permanent disability.

This means that the tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence:
 (i) Whether the disablement is  permanent or temporary;
 (ii) If the disablement is permanent,
whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement;
(iii) If the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb,
then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,
that is the permanent disability suffered by the person.
If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent disability then there is no question of proceeding further and determining the loss of future earning capacity.
But if the Tribunal concludes that there is permanent disability then it will SHAILENDER MALIK MACT No.213/2018

MALIK Date:
2024.02.16 Page 10 16:05:19 +0530 proceed to ascertain its extent.

After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The tribunal has to first ascertain what activities of the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) Whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood."

sentences.text: If doctor has given evidence about percentage of permanent disability, Tribunal will have to seek doctors opinion as to whether it is possible to deduce the corresponding functional permanent disability with reference to whole body and if so to what percentage.
13. We may now summarize the principles discussed above:
(i). All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.

(ii). The percentage of permanent MACT No.213/2018 by SHAILENDER  SHAILENDER MALIK  MALIK  Page 11  Date: 2024.02.16  16:05:33 +0530 disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.

To put it differently, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability (except in a few cases, where the Tribunal on the basis of evidence, concludes that percentage of loss of earning capacity is the same as percentage of permanent disability).

(iii). The doctor who treated an injured- claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.

(iv). The same permanent disability may result in different percentages of loss of earning capacity in different persons, depending upon the nature of profession, occupation or job, age, education and other factors."
24.

Keeping in view the ratio as discussed above, petitioner has examined PW2 Dr.Siddharth Pathak, Senior Resident, Orthopedics, GTB Hospital who deposed regarding medical disability certificate dated 02.06.2022 of petitioner Sonu Gautam as Ex.PW2/1.
PW2 states that as per disability certificate petitioner suffered 25% permanent disability relation to his left lower limb.
During cross examination PW2 stated that he cannot comment upon the functional disability of whole body of patient.
He also stated that he cannot tell whether the patient can drive the vehicle.

25. The disablement and loss of earning capacity are two SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK MACT No.213/2018 Page 12 Date: 2024.02.16 16:05:41 +0530 different aspects and may not corresponding to each other and the loss of income has to be seen considering the profession in which the petitioner was engaged at the time of accident.
It has come in the evidence that petitioner was suffering from 25% disability in relation to left lower limb.

PW2 in his cross-examination however admitted that he cannot comment on the extent of functional disability of the petitioner,

however PW2 stated that patient/petitioner would face difficulty in plain surface, walking on slope,
climbing stairs and squatting.
Although it is not proved that petitioner was actually working as taxi driver.

But at the same time taking into consideration evidence of PW2 Dr.Siddharth Pathak, this Tribunal is of considered view that the functional disability of petitioner must be 50% of medical disability, in view of the evidence of PW2 as noted above.

In such circumstances this Tribunal finds that the functional disability to whole body of the petitioner may be considered to be 12.5% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of his future income.

26. Further, law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also [refer:
Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351].

Thus,
considering the petitioner being below 40 years at the time of accident, an addition of income to the extent of 40% towards future prospects has to be counted.

27. As discussed above, the income of the petitioner has been assessed as Rs.16,182/- + 40%
(Rs.6,473/-), total Rs.22,655/- (Rs.16,182 + Rs.6,473).
Thus applying the functional disability to be 12.5% of Rs.22,655/-, amount comes out to be Rs.2,832/-.
As such the loss of future income due to disability comes out to be Rs.2,832 X 12 X 18 = Rs.6,11,712/-.

NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Pain & Sufferings:
30.

While discussing the criteria to ascertain the compensation for pain and sufferings by victim of vehicular accident, observations of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No: 709/02, date of decision:
02.02.2007 can be considered:
"12. On account of pain and suffering, suffice would it be to note that it is difficult to measure pain and suffering in terms of a money value.
However, compensation which has to be paid must bear some objectives co-relation with the pain and suffering.

13. The objective facts relatable to pain and suffering would be:
(a) Nature of injury.
(b) Body part affected (c) Duration of the treatment."
31.
In this case, as per medical documents of petitioner, he was found to have suffered grievous injuries i.e. multiple fractures and abrasions on different parts of his body.

Treatment record of petitioner shows that due to accidental injuries he SHAILENDER MALIK MACT No.213/2018 MALIK Date: 2024.02.16 16:06:44 +0530 Page 15 remain under medical treatment for about two month as he has been taking treatment from GTB Hospital and Arogya Hospital, Vaishali,
Ghaziabad on number of occasions.

Thus, it is clear that petitioner must have suffered immense pain and suffering during his treatment and therefore, I am of the opinion that an amount of Rs.50,000/- would be just and fair compensation for pain, sufferings and mental trauma suffered by the petitioner as consequences of injuries sustained in the accident.
Accordingly, Rs.50,000/- is granted to the petitioner under this head.

opennyai_summary.issue:
On the basis of pleadings as come on the record ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal on 04.05.2018 framed following issues :
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offendig vehicle bearing no. DL1E 2115 on 10.07.2017 at about 12.15 pm at Loni Road opposite petrol pump, Jyoti Nagar, in rash and negligent manner and caused injuries to Sonu?
OPP (2)Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, for what amount and from whom?
The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so, the extent of such permanent disability.
This means that the tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence:
 (i) Whether the disablement is  permanent or temporary;
 (ii) If the disablement is permanent,
whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement;
(iii) If the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb,
then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,
that is the permanent disability suffered by the person.
If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent disability then there is no question of proceeding further and determining the loss of future earning capacity.
After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
The tribunal has to first ascertain what activities of the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) Whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood."

However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the claim petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others.
14. Thus considering the evidence as come on the judicial record, this Tribunal finds that evidence of PW1 is specific and cogent, gets corroboration from the documents filed with DAR including report u/s 173 Cr.PC, seizure memo, notice u/s 133 M.V. Act, site plan as well as mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle.
As such it can safely be concluded that accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of driver/respondent no.1 while driving tractor no.DL-1E-2115.
The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.
Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.
The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK MACT No.213/2018 Page 6 Date: 2024.02.16 16:04:43 +0530 damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
As such petitioner is Dar- Sonu Gautam vs Avadhveer Singh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43808257/
6 entitled for sum of Rs.32,364/- (Rs.16,182 X 2) for loss of earning during treatment.
Although it is not proved that petitioner was actually working as taxi driver.
But at the same time taking into consideration evidence of PW2 Dr.Siddharth Pathak, this Tribunal is of considered view that the functional disability of petitioner must be 50% of medical disability, in view of the evidence of PW2 as noted above.
In such circumstances this Tribunal finds that the functional disability to whole body of the petitioner may be considered to be 12.5% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of his future income.
26. Further, law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also [refer:
Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351].
Accident in the present case occurred on 10.07.2017.
As such age of petitioner as per Ex.PW1/3 on the date of accident was 21 years 10 months.
As such multiplier to be applied in the present case would be 18 as applicable to age group between 21 to 25 years, would be applicable as per settled principle laid down in case of Sarla Verma v.
DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121.
Moreover, the law has been SHAILENDER MALIK MACT No.213/2018 MALIK Date:
 2024.02.16 Page 13  16:05:49 +0530 well settled by the decisions of Supreme Court in the cases of Sandeep Khanuja (supra) and Erudhaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd. 2020 SCC OnLine SC 601, that while applying the multiplier method, future prospects on advancement in life and career are also to be taken into consideration.
Thus,
considering the petitioner being below 40 years at the time of accident, an addition of income to the extent of 40% towards future prospects has to be counted.
This Tribunal while assessing medical condition of the accused, granted the petitioner loss of earning during treatment for two months.
In such situation, in view of evidence of PW1, documents place on record and other material, this Tribunal finds it appropriate to grant Rs.15,000/- each under the head of special diet and conveyance charges.
Thus, it is clear that petitioner must have suffered immense pain and suffering during his treatment and therefore, I am of the opinion that an amount of Rs.50,000/- would be just and fair compensation for pain, sufferings and mental trauma suffered by the petitioner as consequences of injuries sustained in the accident.
It is evident on record that even after completion of treatment, petitioner suffered permanent medical disability of 25% in relation to his left lower limb which has been assessed as 12.5%
functional disability in relation to whole body of the petitioner by this Tribunal.
